nodes.title: Swap in any picture of your own
Note
widgets_values:
# TEST: EPS Resolution - one node for the resize, and sizes you can save

**Just press Run.** No checkpoint, no lora, no GPU. It loads a picture,
resizes it to 1024 x 1024 and saves the result. A second, maybe.

One node does the resize *and* reports the numbers, so you are not wiring up
a resize node, a reroute and a get-size node to do one obvious thing.

## Pass 1 - the basics

Run once as it ships: `output/eps_restest/size_00001_.png`, 1024 x 1024,
squashed. Squashed is what **stretch** means.

Now try each of these and Run again:

- **resize_method -> keep aspect (fit)** - fits inside the box, no squash.
- **crop to fill** - fills the box and trims the overflow.
- **pad** - fits inside the box and fills the gap with black.
- **height -> 0** - leave width at 1024 and the height works itself out from
  the picture's own shape. Both at 0 keeps the original size.
- **multiple_of -> 64** - rounds the result to a number samplers are happy
  with. This is the setting that heads off "your image is 1023 pixels tall"
  before it happens.

Drag inside the pad on the node to set width and height by feel. The readout
below it shows `W x H`, the aspect ratio and the megapixels while you drag.
**copy from image** fills width and height with the wired picture's own size
in one click.

## Pass 2 - presets, which is the actual point

Set a size you like and press **Save** on the node. Give it a name. It now
lives in your library folder next to your prompt notebooks and lora sets, so
every machine sharing that folder has it.

Now tick **more than one** preset and press Run **once**.

You get one picture per ticked preset, out of a single queue. Two presets,
two files. Five, five. Same source, same everything else - just every size
you care about, in one go. That is the whole reason to save sizes rather
than retype them. Edit any field by hand and the ticked preset un-selects
itself, so the numbers you see are the numbers that run.

**This workflow ships with nothing ticked**, so it runs on a fresh install
without you setting anything up first.

If you would rather not type presets in, `eps-resolution-test-presets.json`
sits next to this file with two ready-made ones (`Square 1024` and
`Portrait 832`). That one is **not a workflow** - do not drag it onto the
canvas. If you have no `resolution_presets.json` in your library folder yet,
copy it in there under that name. **If you already have one, do
not overwrite it** - just make the two by hand with Save. It takes ten
seconds and you will not lose the presets you already had.

## The one gotcha

A ticked preset that no longer exists **fails the run**, on purpose, with a
message naming it. That is deliberate: quietly falling back to some other
size would mean shipping the wrong pictures and never finding out. If you
renamed or deleted a preset on another machine, untick it here.

## Hiding in Properties

Right-click the node -> Properties.

- **Show passthrough image** brings back the untouched original on the first
  output, for when you want both sizes downstream.
- **Show original size** adds the before-resize width and height as two more
  outputs.
- **Show grid** and **Grid max** control the drag pad.

Both extra outputs are off here to keep the node small.

widgets_values:
## What comes out

`resized_image` is the one you want - it is wired to Save Image.

`width` and `height` are the size *after* the resize, ready to feed an Empty
Latent or a note-to-self. Wire them somewhere and you never have to do the
arithmetic yourself.

The first output, `image`, is the original untouched - hidden here to keep
the node tidy. Turn it back on in Properties if you want both.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values:
## One preset in, one file out

Nothing ticked - which is how this ships - means one run at whatever width
and height the widgets say.

Tick two presets and this same Save Image writes two files from one Run, one
per size. Tick five and you get five. The node fans out; nothing downstream
has to know.
